title: The Great Emu War — Australia lost a war to birds in 1932
hook: AUSTRALIA LOST A WAR TO BIRDS
voiceover: In 1932, Australia declared war on emus. Tens of thousands of the giant flightless birds were destroying crops in Western Australia. The government sent in soldiers. With machine guns. The emus, it turned out, were surprisingly hard to kill. They scattered. They ran zigzag. They could take multiple bullets and keep going. The military expedition fired thousands of rounds. The official report admitted maybe a few hundred emus died. The leader called the birds invulnerable, like Zulu warriors. After six weeks, the army quietly withdrew. Australia. Lost. A war. To birds. Follow Mindbloom for one fact a day.
